case_name: State of Assam v Ramesh Chandra Dey and Others
facts: This appeal has been filed by the State of Assam against a judgment of the High Court of Assam dated July 16, 1956.
R. C. Dey, the answering respondent, is a wholesale dealer in tea, and has been in business since 1949.
He registered himself as a dealer under the Assam Sales Tax Act on January 14, 1950.
In respect of tea sold in Calcutta, R. C. Dey consigns the tea to himself after purchasing it in Assam.
This tea is then approved by prospective purchasers, to whom the documents of title are endorsed on receipt of the price.
issues: Whether s. 15 of the Assam Sales Tax Act, 1947, and Rule 80 framed under the Act were ultra vires, being a breach of Art. 286(2) of the Constitution.
Whether the amendment to s. 15 and the Rules affected inter-State trade or commerce directly or indirectly.
petitioner_arguments: The amendment and the Rule were void as offending Art. 19 (1)(g).
The amendment and the Rule had the effect of taxing sales in the course of inter-State trade or commerce and were, therefore, illegal.
court_reasoning: Only sales which affected inter-State trade or commerce directly and were an integral part thereof, were saved under Art. 286(2).
The transactions of sales which have been taxed were wholly inside the State of Orissa.
The present levy is not on the sales by the petitioner to persons outside the State, but on the purchases by him inside the State.
What s. 15 does, is to grant an additional exemption in respect of sales in which the goods, though sold to a registered dealer, are meant for resale in the State, itself.
holding: The High Court held that s. 15 of the Assam Sales Tax Act, 1947, and Rule 80 framed under the Act were ultra vires, being a breach of Art. 286(2) of the Constitution.
The amendment to s. 15 and the Rules did not affect inter-State trade or commerce directly or indirectly.
